assertions: He will not obtain the desired parsonage / benefice
His suit for the parsonage will fail despite his pressing it and despite ignoring advice to desist
Saturn impedited in the Ascendant infortunes the question: the matter is blocked, delayed and frustrated from the querent's own side, and his covetous disposition harms his cause
No perfection is possible: Jupiter, lord of the 9th and significator of the benefice, makes no aspect to the lord of the Ascendant nor to the Moon, and there is no reception between the significators
Neither the lord of the Ascendant nor the Moon is placed in the 9th, and there is no translation or collection of light to connect querent to benefice
The Moon separating from a trine and applying to an opposition of Mercury, lord of the 3rd, brings hindrance through opposition, adverse report, writing, message or third-house persons/matters
Venus in the 7th opposing the Ascendant shows an opposing party / rival standing against him in the matter
He will not by this parsonage restore the good place and former credit he had lately lost; he must look elsewhere for his living
summary: He will not obtain the desired parsonage; the suit is wholly impedited with no connection between his significators and the lord of the 9th benefice.
method: Classical horary astrology per William Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II (whole-sign/traditional testimonies: significators, aspect, reception, translation/collection of light, Moon's application, Saturn in Ascendant)
reasoning: Querent = lord of Ascendant + Moon; benefice = lord of 9th Jupiter. All perfection testimonies are absent: no aspect, no reception, no translation/collection, neither querent significator in 9th. Saturn impedited in Ascendant infortunes the question. Moon applies to opposition of Mercury lord of 3rd (hindrance/opposition) and Venus in 7th opposes Ascendant (adversary). Seven negative testimonies converge on denial.
